findings.summary: EVENT_NOP passes describeUnknownEvent(statusByte) as description, producing 'Unknown Event: 0xNN' for a known NOP event
findings.failure_scenario: When parsing any HudsonSnes sequence file, every NOP byte encountered produces UI output like 'NOP' with description 'Unknown Event: 0xNN', misidentifying a known event as unknown. This is wrong because NOP is a defined event, not an unknown opcode.

findings.summary: EVENT_NOP1 passes describeUnknownEvent(statusByte) as description for a known NOP event
findings.failure_scenario: Same as EVENT_NOP above: every NOP1 byte (status byte with 1 arg consumed as padding) produces 'NOP' with misleading 'Unknown Event: 0xNN' description.

findings.summary: EVENT_NOTE tie branch passes describeUnknownEvent(statusByte) for a known note tie, producing 'Unknown Event' description
findings.failure_scenario: When two identical consecutive notes are slurred (tied), the Tie event gets description 'Unknown Event: 0xNN', confusing users who see a Tie with an 'Unknown' label.
Every loop end in a HudsonSnes sequence displays 'Loop End' with description 'Unknown Event: 0xNN'. A known control flow event is mislabeled as unknown, making debugging loop logic harder.
Echo enable events show 'Echo On' with misleading 'Unknown Event: 0xNN' description. Echo On is a defined, known SPC700 DSP event.
Disabling the pitch attack envelope produces 'Attack Pitch Envelope Off' with 'Unknown Event: 0xNN' description. This is a known, named event.
Infinite loop point markers show 'Infinite Loop Point' with 'Unknown Event: 0xNN' description. This is a known song structure event, not unknown.
One-shot infinite loop point markers show 'Infinite Loop Point (Ignore after the Second Time)' with misleading 'Unknown Event: 0xNN' description.
